---
title: "Delayed mode in NRT products"
format:
  html:
    page-layout: full
execute:
  echo: false
---

A flag set in delayed mode is likely to be an operator's decision rather
than an automated test's, so comparing it with nrtqclib asks a different
question from comparing two sets of NRT flags. The rest of the site already
keeps profiles with a delayed mode observation apart, by the data mode the
files declare. This page adds a group the files do not declare: **profiles
marked NRT whose flags look like delayed mode ones.**

The page covers the NRT products only. CORA is left out: the rest of the
site files it whole as delayed mode, since its flags come from its own
delayed mode QC, so it has no profile marked NRT to estimate. The delayed
mode profiles below are the ones the NRT products declare.

The sign is the share of a profile's observations that the input flags and
nrtqclib does not. An automated test rarely rejects most of a profile; an
operator who judges a cast bad often rejects all of it. Delayed mode
profiles show it, and so do some profiles marked real time.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false"}
```{ojs}
meta ? md`**The estimated delayed mode profiles are defined with a threshold of ${percent(rule.min_share)}.** A profile marked NRT${rule.groups.includes("unknown") ? ", or with no data mode," : ""} is estimated to be delayed mode for a variable when at least ${percent(rule.min_share)} of its observations of that variable with a usable input flag are flagged by the input and not by nrtqclib. The variable counts only with at least ${rule.min_observations} such observations, so a short profile, where a few flagged values make a large share, is not called.

Every page of the site that shows the estimated delayed mode group uses this threshold, the dashboard included. The threshold is a setting of the analysis: the figure and table under "How much the threshold matters" try others, to show how much the choice changes the count, and nothing else depends on them.` : html``
```
:::

**Temperature and salinity are judged apart.** An operator often reworks
one and leaves the other alone, and most of the profiles this finds are
reworked in salinity only. So a profile can be estimated delayed mode for
salinity and still be NRT for temperature: it leaves the salinity
comparison and stays in the temperature one. Every table and figure below
has the two variables apart.

```{ojs}
//| output: false
app = import(new URL("assets/js/app.js", document.baseURI).href)
meta = app.loadAnalyses()
name = (id) => app.datasetName(meta, id)
table = app.analysisTable
byDataset = (a, b) => app.datasetOrder(meta, a.dataset_id) - app.datasetOrder(meta, b.dataset_id)
rule = meta ? meta.rules.estimated_delayed : null
groupLabel = (key) => meta.groups.find((g) => g.key === key)?.label ?? key
modeLabel = (key) => meta.data_modes.find((m) => m.key === key)?.label ?? key
variableLabel = (n) => meta.variables.find((v) => v.name === n)?.label ?? n
variableOrder = (n) => meta.variables.findIndex((v) => v.name === n)
byDatasetVariable = (a, b) => byDataset(a, b) || variableOrder(a.variable) - variableOrder(b.variable)
percent = (value) => `${Math.round(100 * value)}%`
```

```{ojs}
meta === null ? app.analysesMissing() : html``
```

## The groups

Profiles the bathymetry puts on land are left out first: they are the
subject of the [Depth](analyses-depth.qmd) page, and nothing on this page
or the next counts them. For each variable, every profile at sea is then
filed under exactly one group, decided in this order: containing delayed
mode, estimated delayed mode, data mode unknown, and NRT. Only the last is
compared item by item on [Flag differences](analyses-flags.qmd), each
variable over its own NRT profiles.

```{ojs}
groupsTable = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("dm_groups") : null
// The groups at sea that hold any profile: an empty one would be a blank column.
seaGroups = meta && groupsTable
  ? meta.groups.filter((g) => g.key !== "land" && groupsTable.some((r) => r.group === g.key && r.n_profiles > 0))
  : []
groupRows = groupsTable
  ? app.widen(groupsTable.filter((r) => r.group !== "land"), { index: ["dataset_id", "variable"], column: "group", value: "n_profiles" })
      .map((r) => ({ ...r, key: `${r.dataset_id}|${r.variable}`, n_sea: seaGroups.reduce((sum, g) => sum + (r[g.key] ?? 0), 0) }))
      .sort(byDatasetVariable)
  : []
meta ? table(groupRows, [
  { key: "dataset_id", label: "Product", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "variable", label: "Variable", align: "left", format: variableLabel },
  { key: "n_sea", label: "Profiles at sea" },
  ...seaGroups.map((g) => ({ key: g.key, label: g.label, title: g.description }))
]) : html``
```

```{ojs}
meta ? app.analysisFigure(
  "dm_groups",
  "Each product's profiles at sea by the group the analyses file them under, one panel per variable; the number of profiles at sea is in brackets. Profiles on land are left out (see Depth): a small share of most products, but more in the Baltic.",
  "Stacked bars of the share of profiles in each group, per product."
) : html``
```

## The share flagged by the input alone

```{ojs}
meta ? app.analysisFigure(
  "dm_share",
  `Profiles by the share of their observations of each variable flagged by the input alone, coloured by the data mode their files declare: one row per product, one column per variable. Profiles with no such observation, most of every product, are left out and counted in the table below. The dashed line is the threshold, ${percent(rule.min_share)}.`,
  "Histograms of the input-only share per product and variable, split by declared data mode."
) : html``
```

The shares are two humps: profiles where the input flags a few values
nrtqclib does not, and profiles where it flags nearly all of them, many at
exactly 100%. The second hump is larger in salinity than in temperature in
most products. The threshold sits between them, at a clear majority of the
profile rather than half of it, since an automated test can plausibly
reject half a profile.

```{ojs}
meta ? md`**How much the threshold matters.** The estimated delayed mode profiles on this site are those at or above ${percent(rule.min_share)}. The figure tries other thresholds, for comparison only: for each product and variable, how many profiles the rule would estimate to be delayed mode at each threshold from 50% to 100%. A flat line means the choice hardly matters there, because the input alone flags those profiles almost in full or hardly at all. A falling line means many profiles sit between the two humps, and the threshold decides how many of them are estimated.` : html``
```

```{ojs}
meta ? app.analysisFigure(
  "dm_threshold",
  `Profiles marked NRT${rule.groups.includes("unknown") ? ", or with no data mode," : ""} that the rule would estimate to be delayed mode, at each threshold from 50% to 100%: one panel per product and variable. Each panel has its own scale, starting at zero, so the fall of a line is its real proportion. The large point and the vertical line mark the threshold in use, ${percent(rule.min_share)}, with the number of profiles it estimates.`,
  "Line charts per product and variable of the number of profiles estimated delayed mode against the threshold."
) : html``
```

The salinity of the Arctic regional product is flat: its estimated
profiles are flagged almost in full. The salinity of the Arctic global
product and the temperature of the Mediterranean global product fall
steadily, so there the threshold matters. The Baltic and the Mediterranean
regional product have few estimated profiles, and a step of one or two
profiles looks steep.

The table gives the same counts, with a row for the profiles whose files
declare delayed mode where a product has any.

```{ojs}
thresholds = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("dm_threshold") : null
hist = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("dm_share_hist") : null
thresholdRows = thresholds
  ? app.widen(thresholds, { index: ["dataset_id", "variable", "data_mode", "n_eligible"], column: "threshold", value: "n_profiles", name: (t) => `t${t}` })
      .map((row) => ({
        ...row,
        key: `${row.dataset_id}|${row.variable}|${row.data_mode}`,
        zero: (hist ?? []).filter((h) => h.dataset_id === row.dataset_id && h.variable === row.variable && h.data_mode === row.data_mode && h.bin_hi === 0)
          .reduce((s, h) => s + h.n_profiles, 0)
      }))
      .sort((a, b) => byDatasetVariable(a, b) || a.data_mode.localeCompare(b.data_mode))
  : []
thresholdKeys = thresholds ? [...new Set(thresholds.map((t) => t.threshold))].sort((a, b) => a - b) : []
meta ? table(thresholdRows, [
  { key: "dataset_id", label: "Product", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "variable", label: "Variable", align: "left", format: variableLabel },
  { key: "data_mode", label: "Declared", align: "left", format: modeLabel },
  { key: "n_eligible", label: "With a share", title: `Profiles with at least ${rule.min_observations} observations of the variable with a usable input flag` },
  { key: "zero", label: "Share 0" },
  ...thresholdKeys.map((t) => ({ key: `t${t}`, label: `At or above ${percent(t)}` }))
]) : html``
```

The rows of profiles that declare delayed mode are a check on the rule,
and only the Arctic products hold enough of them. In the Arctic global
product, the declared ones that reach 50% nearly all reach 90% too, while
the profiles marked NRT thin out much more as the threshold rises: a
profile marked NRT with a share between 50% and 90% looks less like an
operator's work than one above it, which is why the threshold is not set
lower. In the Arctic regional product both stay nearly flat.

## What the estimate takes out of NRT

The [Flag differences](analyses-flags.qmd) page compares nrtqclib with the
input over the NRT profiles only, so the estimated profiles are not in it.
The table shows what that removes, for each product and variable: the share
of the observations flagged by the input and not by nrtqclib ("original
only"), with the estimated profiles counted as NRT and without them, and
how many of those flags were in the estimated profiles.

The estimated profiles are a small part of every product, but they hold a
large part of its original-only flags: most of them in the salinity of the
Arctic products, a smaller part elsewhere. The flags nrtqclib sets, alone
or with the input, hardly change.

```{ojs}
// Original-only flags of the NRT group, with the estimated profiles added
// back and without them.
removedRows = groupsTable
  ? [...groupsTable
      .filter((r) => r.group === "nrt" || r.group === "estimated_delayed")
      .reduce((m, r) => {
        const key = `${r.dataset_id}|${r.variable}`;
        const row = m.get(key) ?? { key, dataset_id: r.dataset_id, variable: r.variable, n_estimated: 0, n_obs: 0, n_obs_nrt: 0, n_flags: 0, n_flags_nrt: 0 };
        const nrt = r.group === "nrt";
        if (!nrt) row.n_estimated += r.n_profiles;
        row.n_obs += r.n_obs;
        row.n_flags += r.n_original_only;
        if (nrt) { row.n_obs_nrt += r.n_obs; row.n_flags_nrt += r.n_original_only; }
        m.set(key, row);
        return m;
      }, new Map()).values()]
      .map((r) => ({ ...r, n_flags_estimated: r.n_flags - r.n_flags_nrt }))
      .sort(byDatasetVariable)
  : []
meta ? table(removedRows, [
  { key: "dataset_id", label: "Product", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "variable", label: "Variable", align: "left", format: variableLabel },
  { key: "n_estimated", label: "Estimated profiles" },
  { key: "n_flags", label: "Original only, with them", title: "Share of the observations flagged by the input and not by nrtqclib, with the estimated profiles counted as NRT", format: (_, r) => app.formatSmallShare(r.n_flags, r.n_obs) },
  { key: "n_flags_nrt", label: "Original only, without them", title: "The same share over the NRT profiles alone, as compared on Flag differences", format: (_, r) => app.formatSmallShare(r.n_flags_nrt, r.n_obs_nrt) },
  { key: "n_flags_estimated", label: "Held by the estimated profiles", title: "Share of the original-only flags above that were in the estimated profiles", format: (_, r) => app.formatShare(r.n_flags_estimated, r.n_flags) }
]) : html``
```

## Where they come from

If the estimate picks up reprocessing rather than chance, its profiles
should gather on a few platforms instead of spreading thinly. For each
platform and variable with any: how many of its profiles could be
estimated (marked NRT or with no data mode), how many were, and how many it
has in declared delayed mode.

```{ojs}
platforms = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("dm_estimated_platforms") : null
meta ? table((platforms ?? []).map((r) => ({ ...r, key: `${r.dataset_id}|${r.variable}|${r.platform_code}` })).sort((a, b) => b.n_estimated - a.n_estimated), [
  { key: "dataset_id", label: "Product", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "variable", label: "Variable", align: "left", format: variableLabel },
  { key: "platform_code", label: "Platform", align: "left", format: (v) => v },
  { key: "n_profiles", label: "Profiles at sea" },
  { key: "n_candidates", label: "NRT or unknown" },
  { key: "n_estimated", label: "Estimated" },
  { key: "share", label: "Share", format: (_, r) => app.formatShare(r.n_estimated, r.n_candidates) },
  { key: "n_delayed", label: "Declared delayed" }
]) : html``
```

Every profile estimated for either variable is listed, with its share and
estimate per variable, in
[the table this page reads](data/analyses/tables/dm_estimated_profiles.csv).
